claims.text: CALPHAD can identify stable phases and phase equilibria in multicomponent alloys.
CALPHAD can accurately predict the phonon thermal conductivity of high-entropy alloys.
The thermal conductivities corresponding to CALPHAD-predicted phases can be identified.
The approach applies under high-temperature conditions.
The approach applies to alloys containing multiple elements at similar concentrations.
Phase stability and solid-solution formation are the structural mediators relevant to the prediction.
CALPHAD uses thermodynamic calculations and energy minimization to predict phase equilibria.
The most stable phases determine the phonon thermal conductivity of a high-entropy alloy.
The CALPHAD-based approach will improve prediction of phonon thermal conductivity.
The improved prediction will enable identification of high-entropy alloys with low thermal conductivity.
Current experimental measurements constitute the baseline against which the predictive approach is compared.
CALPHAD requires accurate thermodynamic databases and computational software.
Uncertainty in predicted phase stability and solid-solution formation can reduce the accuracy of phonon thermal-conductivity predictions.
Experimental phonon thermal conductivity, phase composition, and microstructure can be measured to test the prediction.
A mismatch between predicted and experimentally measured phonon thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The outcome claims improvement in prediction, but the stated baseline is an experimental measurement method rather than a current predictive method, so the proposed improvement is not defined against a comparable baseline.
